design_evaluation.summary: A polished dark-themed landing page with a clear hero-to-tools hierarchy, functioning navigation, theme toggle, login modal, and AI chat with a consent gate. Main weaknesses are floating widgets (Voice Agent / AI chat button) overlapping and truncating card content on desktop and mobile, several low-contrast secondary labels, and a lack of visible affordances (chat panel has no header or close control).
strengths: Strong hero hierarchy: large two-tone headline, supporting paragraph, stats row, and dual CTAs (Live Feed / AI Lab) read in a clear top-down order on desktop.
Consistent dark visual system across nav, hero, cards, and mockup window; the terminal/AI-test-result mockup effectively reinforces the product's testing theme.
Mobile menu is clean: logo, login, and close button retained in the header, nav items comfortably spaced, and 'Break it' accent item matches the desktop highlight.
Theme toggle works with a coherent light-mode palette (light background, dark text, dark code mockup retained), demonstrating a real dual-theme design rather than inverted colors.
Login modal has clear tabbed Login/Register state, labeled Email/Password fields, primary gradient CTA, and a discoverable 'Forgot password?' link; the blurred backdrop focuses attention.
Chat opens with a responsible consent screen ('Before we start', AI disclaimer, checkbox, disabled-looking 'Agree & Start Chat' button gated on agreement), which is clear interaction sequencing.
Tool cards use uniform structure (icon, title, description, action link with arrows) with color-coded accent icons, aiding scannability.
issues: Floating Voice Agent pill and circular AI button overlap and obscure card content: the 'Reliability & Fact Check' description is clipped ('...unsupported AI claims' runs under the widget) on desktop, and on mobile they cover the 'Adversarial Simulation' card text entirely.
The vertical 'LIVE' badge bleeds off the left edge and overlaps the hero area; its tiny rotated text is decorative at best and sits over content in light mode too.
The chat panel (ui-chat-opens) has no visible header, title, or close control; users cannot see how to dismiss the panel, and it fully covers the hero's right-side mockup.

Contrast concerns: stat labels ('ARTICLES TODAY', 'RSS SOURCES', 'AUTO-UPDATED'), card descriptions, and the badge text 'AI Integration & Quality Management' are low-contrast against the dark gradient; in light mode, card descriptions also appear washed out.

Accessibility cues are weak: no visible focus/keyboard indicators in any screenshot, icon-only controls (settings gear, modal X) have no visible labels or tooltips, and the modal does not visibly indicate aria/focus-trap affordances.
Theme toggle icon shows a moon while in light mode, which is ambiguous; convention typically shows the mode you'd switch to (sun in light mode is acceptable, but paired with no label it's unclear).
Mobile menu background does not fully dim or lock the page beneath consistently — hero stats and floating widgets remain visually active under the open menu, which can look like broken layering.
Nav 'Break it' button uses a skull icon with red styling that reads as destructive/danger; its purpose is unclear from the label alone.
Stats values differ across screenshots (26 vs 8 vs 50 'ARTICLES TODAY') with no timestamp or source context, which may appear inconsistent to users.

candidate_findings.expected: Request is rejected without proxying; response is a controlled JSON error (4xx) and body contains no internal page content, secrets, or stack trace.

However, the response status is 200 instead of the expected 4xx (400/403/422), so expected_status_match is false. The rejection is signaled only in the body while the transport layer reports success, which violates the documented error contract and can mislead clients, caches, and monitoring into treating the block as a successful fetch.
reproduction_steps: Compare the sanitized response with the declared semantic contract.
